text:
Jack Quinn is having the season Buffalo drafted him eighth overall for. He has 13 goals and 24 points in 24 games, goals in three straight (four in all), and a two-goal night in the 6-3 win in Washington on Nov. 19. A Substack headline this week was blunt: "Sabres Need to Pay Jack Quinn ASAP."

The role changed first. He's playing 18:44 a night, up from 15:39, and he's on the ice for 80% of the Sabres' power-play chances after 37% last season. His own chances rose with it, to 1.20 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his shots) from 0.96, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season.

Some of the finish is borrowed. He has 13 goals on 9.0 expected, shooting 19% after 10% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. His minutes have also slipped 1:17 a night over the last ten. Evolving-Hockey flagged his defense last season (bottom 2% of forwards in chances allowed), so watch the other end while the role holds.
